about: sedi-1's issuer cases (test-plan item 4, choice issuer-issues): each case is an acdc.issue request over a schema of the suite's own, and either the issuance the runner verifies or the refusal an issuer must give. The named SEDI credentials follow once acdc.issue can carry rules and nested attribute blocks.

cases.title: A credential issued to its holder
cases.description: The issuer issues one credential to the holder under a blindable registry of its own. A sedi-1 issuer issues it, and the runner verifies every KEL, registry event and the ACDC it returns.

cases.title: An untargeted credential
cases.description: As SI-01, but the credential names no issuee, so its attribute block carries no i. A sedi-1 issuer issues it.

cases.title: A credential with an I2I edge that holds
cases.description: The issuer issues core to the holder, and the holder issues guardian with an I2I edge to core; the edge holds, since core's issuee issues guardian. A sedi-1 issuer issues both.

cases.title: An attribute the schema forbids
cases.description: As SI-01, but the request adds an attribute the schema's closed attribute section does not name. A sedi-1 issuer refuses, rather than issue a credential its own schema refuses.
cases.triage: Issuing it puts into circulation a credential no verifier that checks its schema accepts.
expect: request refused/the attributes of core do not satisfy its schema

cases.title: An I2I edge that cannot hold
cases.description: As SI-03, but core is issued to a third identifier, other, so an I2I edge from guardian, which the holder issues, cannot hold. A sedi-1 issuer refuses.
cases.triage: Issuing it asserts a chain of authority its own edge says does not hold.
expect: request refused/the edges of guardian cannot hold as the request issues them

cases.title: An NI2I edge to a credential issued elsewhere
cases.description: The issuer issues core to a third identifier, other, and the holder issues guardian with an NI2I edge to core. NI2I does not bind the issuers, so the edge holds though core's issuee does not issue guardian. A sedi-1 issuer issues both.

cases.title: An identity assurance receipt, issued directly
cases.description: The issuer issues a credential to the holder under a schema that closes its top level without an rd, as SEDI's identity assurance receipt schema does, and asks for no registry. A sedi-1 issuer issues it with no rd and anchors the digest seal of its SAID in its KEL.

cases.title: No registry under a schema that admits one
cases.description: As SI-07, but under a schema whose top level admits an rd. Only a credential whose schema forbids rd is issued directly, so a sedi-1 issuer refuses.
cases.triage: Issuing it puts into circulation a credential no verifier can find committed, and one its issuer can never revoke.
expect: request refused/the schema of receipt admits a registry, so it cannot be issued without one

cases.title: A registry under a schema that forbids rd
cases.description: As SI-07, but the request asks for a blindable registry. The schema forbids rd, so the credential could not name its registry and still satisfy its schema, and a sedi-1 issuer refuses.
cases.triage: Issuing it gives a credential that fails its own schema, or a registry the credential never names.
expect: request refused/the schema of receipt forbids rd, so it cannot name a registry
